Gor Vazumbrog (西山驿, I14)

Scoring-table region: Serpentspine.

One-line positioning: Return to the Titanium Dwarves' vault ruined by a dragon, and turn monster hunters, golems, and expeditions into the tools of national restoration.

Story: high | Mission-tree length: long (37 direct missions) | Mission-tree freshness: local mission file modified 2026-09-07, Mod support v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: very high | Waiting burden: high | Early pressure: medium-high | Expansion capacity: medium-high.

Identity and the Old Hold

Gor Vazumbrog is the current localized name of I14. It is a country formed through the generic Dwarven adventurer hold decision after reclaiming its ancestral home. Formation requires control of province 4217, where Gor Vazumbrog stands, together with the adventurer conditions; the adventurer republic, Titanium Dwarf culture, and Ancestor Worship in the country-history file are the post-formation template and do not prove that the country already held the fortress on the 1444 map. The current scripts assign I14 its own mission tree, and no other mandatory successor Tag was confirmed. Different eligible adventurer bands can enter this campaign, so one predecessor's experience must not be written as a fixed opening for every run. [Local script] [Local localization]

Local narrative text presents the old Gor Vazumbrog as the Dwarven Empire's vault: ancient texts, artifacts, experiments, and dangerous inventions were stored there, while the Titanium Orders served as guards and hunters. After the Empire's collapse, the vault was breached; Titanium Dwarves scattered as far as Bulwar, and some took refuge in Seghdihr. The English offline Wiki likewise describes it as a Titanium Dwarf hold in the Middle Serpentspine and records its destruction in a dragon catastrophe during the Dragonwake. The Wiki's ancient history is background evidence, not proof of an uninterrupted legal or political continuity between the old regime and the modern formable country. The player's return after 1444 is the future proposed by this mission tree. [Local narrative text] [Wiki material]

Return, the Dragon's Wound, and Reconstruction

Gor Vazumbrog's story is not merely a mine-hold development line. The opening direction is to reclaim the old hold, repair roads and forward fortresses, bring the exiled Titanium Dwarves home, and rebuild an order capable of facing the monsters of the Serpentspine. The missions first require clearing hostile forces nearby and establishing supply and defenses, then push deeper into the contaminated levels. The ruined vault, poisonous vapors, and lingering magic make the Dragon's Wound a long-term obstacle: restoring the homeland means entering a still-dangerous underground in a planned manner, not simply taking the province and immediately digging to the bottom. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

The restoration also has an unsettling side. The event for rebuilding the monster-hunter order directly applies devastation to owned provinces with Orcish culture, reduces development, changes culture and religion, and lowers tolerance of Orcs. This is a concrete coercive policy in the script; it cannot be summarized merely as “clearing monsters,” and sapient Orcs must not be conflated with hunting targets. The ancient oath in the mission story also uses language about killing all Orcs, but that oath is a character position; the assessment here is based primarily on the actual event effects. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

Four Loops That Define the Experience

The monster hunters and expeditions. After taking the adventurer-estate monster-hunter privilege, the dedicated decision opens the hunt menu. Targets are added progressively through mission flags, geographic control, and completed hunts, while a recent-hunt modifier limits consecutive actions. This ties hold construction, expedition range, and prey preparation together; monster hunting is not a one-click permanent bonus. [Local script]

Roads, fortresses, and supply. Forward fortresses and railway-junction missions turn the Serpentspine routes into military infrastructure. Later objectives also require a sufficient number of road forts and defenses along the mountain frontier. Taking land is only the first step: holding, supplying, and repairing key positions supports further hunts and expansion. If the player pushes outward without building the roads, the mission tree can stall on infrastructure left behind. [Local script]

Golem industry. The missions require magical infrastructure, an operational golem facility, mage loyalty, and supply stations, then increase army golem capacity and upgrade the facilities. Gor Vazumbrog uses magic while treating ancient inventions, workshops, and artificial forces as instruments of national restoration; this is closer to an artificer-led, magic-assisted high-intensity technology route than to a traditional spellcaster state. [Local script]

Vault delves and the Dragon's Wound. “Delve into the vault” requires capital development, workshop output, and multiple completed delves before the exploration range expands; the text also warns that relics are valuable and expeditions may disappear. The Dragon's Wound line first requires refugee return, vermin control, and work in contaminated depths. Both lines turn “wait for the hold to recover” into a real threshold and risk: without economic reserves, construction capacity, and disaster management, valuable relics remain behind sealed doors. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

Stage Goals and Endgame

Before formation, choose a Dwarven adventurer band able to reach province 4217 and ensure that it can seize and hold the site. After formation, prioritize the return of exiles, the monster-hunter privilege, and nearby routes; establish supply capacity, then gradually open distant hunts, golem workshops, and the vault. The mid-tree objective “How to Hurt a Dragon” requires copper, artillery, military strength, and relations with Ovdal Kanzad. Only after it is completed does the artillery order and a war goal against the dragon become available; this is a prepared expedition rather than an opening-day dragon hunt. [Local script]

The final mission, “Stitching the Wound,” requires dragon-hunting spoils, artificer development tools, 5,000 ducats, and magic-assisted construction, then spends that treasury to trigger the concluding event. It brings monster hunting, vault knowledge, and territorial restoration together. The available evidence supports the direction of “stitching the broken homeland,” but does not include a complete in-game run of every mission reward, event branch, or ending; the mission future should therefore not be written as fixed history. [Local script]

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 82/100 | Autocracy 64/100 | Magic↔Artifice 15/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 91/100) | Pluralism 25/100.

The v2.1 values result is Neutral (46/100), with a mixed trajectory. Resettling refugees, repairing transport defenses, and addressing the Dragon's Wound serve public interests. However, the monster-hunter event imposes devastation, development loss, cultural and religious conversion, and reduced tolerance on owned provinces with Orcish culture, harming sapient persons. Conquest, restoration, and artificery do not directly change the values score. Positive and negative actions run through the route, and no phase score difference of about 20 points has been established.

This suits players who enjoy a story-driven Dwarven return, monster-hunting targets, golem industry, dangerous vaults, and medium-to-long construction arcs. Avoid it if you dislike supply and fortress gates, contaminated depths, large late-game treasury requirements, or the route's coercive policy toward Orcs. Two 2026 player experiences report different pacing: a post-release player praised the hunting and magic interaction but found some supply missions repetitive; a development-branch player encountered a chain of Dwarven disasters and debt and abandoned the save. These reflect different versions and circumstances, not a claim that the current stable version is necessarily smooth or necessarily torturous. [Community opinion]

Evidence Boundary

The local scripts determine I14's identity, formation, and mission effects; the English offline Wiki only supplements the ancient hold history, and the current localization determines “西山驿.” A local release announcement confirms that the country once received a new mission tree, but it does not replace the local implementation check. The complete continuity between the ancient Titanium regime and modern formable I14, the best opening adventurer band, every hunt result, and the exact in-game behavior of the final event remain unresolved. Traceable paths are recorded in the evidence file.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. The traditions apply when this idea set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as the idea group is filled, and the ambition applies after all seven ideas are unlocked. Only the national ideas themselves are listed; racial, government, and mission rewards are not mixed in. The ideas adopted on formation are not automatically stacked with the previous set. The idea descriptions may recall history or describe a future ideal; they do not automatically mean that the events had already occurred in 1444.

Gor Vazumbrog (I14) — Titanium Ideas

Traditions: Titanium Traditions

Effects: Tolerance of the True Faith: +2; Trade steering: +20%.

Idea 1: The Titanium Orders

The Titanium Orders refer to the innumerable religious orders of Gor Vazumbrog, the religious warrior-monks, pilgrims, and craftspeople who permeated the fabric of the hold's day-to-day life. Their responsibilities were manyfold, and ranged from guarding the various holy sites and temples around the Dwarovar to carving holy runes and ancestral heroes onto murals.

Others would have small informal groupings of like-minded religious philosophers and guild-monasteries and warrior clans; the Titanium Orders were an informal third faction in the politics of Gor Vazumbrog, alongside the ruling General-King and the Dauvek Veker.

Effects: Global tax modifier: +10%; [Country.GetClergyName] loyalty equilibrium: +5%.

Idea 2: The Vault Hold

In the time of Aul-Dwarov, Gor Vazumbrog was second only to Mithradhûm in matters of military importance and the security of the Dwarovar. It was Gor Vazumbrog that guarded what could not be destroyed, from ancient tomes and relics to new creations deemed too dangerous to enter public usage but too useful to destroy outright.

Cursed artifacts, failed experiments, remnants of Gor Dûrgheled, the many creations or discoveries of Verkal Dromak, Verkal Skomdihr, Hehodovar and Dûr-Vazhatun - all these were sent to Gor Vazumbrog, locked away in a Titanium Vault, and watched over by the hold's guardians until the bitter end. Only by process of appeal to the High King of Amldihr could a vault be opened -and rarely was it done, for much of what was sealed was sealed for good reason.

Effects: Garrison size: +0.3.

Idea 3: Westguard of the Middle Dwarovar

With the fall of Aul-Dwarov and the rise of the Segbandal, Gor Vazumbrog was not left without purpose. Fortifications were built, rebuilt, and expanded, turning the hold into a near impenetrable fortress and the site where dwarfkind made their first real victories against the orc menace. It would be from here, that the Titanium Dwarves attempted the three great Segbandalic Expeditions, attempting to reclaim Hul-Jorkad and Verkal Kozenad.

In addition to the many attempts at reclamation, the Titanium Dwarves also stood stalwart against the endless black tides from the west, the orcs breaking on their walls time and time again. In so doing, they protected the eastern holds and ensured their prosperity for millennia after the old empire's collapse, their stalwart will never breaking against the orcish menace.

Effects: Fort defensiveness: +20%.

Idea 4: Dauvek Veker

Out of the many Titanium Orders, one stood above all others - The Veker-az-Glôbok Dauvek, regularly shortened to Dauvek Veker - the Monster Hunters. Originally a band of death-seeking penitents, the Dauvek Veker evolved into a large guild that often took the front line of offensive and defensive actions during and after the Fall of Aul-Dwarov. Taking on those tasks too big or dangerous for other dwarves to handle, the Dauvek Veker were notoriously fervent, dangerous, and daring.

To join the order, one needed to prove themselves not against mere goblins or orcs, but a great beast of the depths - the Purple Worm was the preferred hunt target for most. As years went on, and supply lines became restricted, the Dauvek Veker evolved further into renowned weaponsmiths, delving the depths of the Dwarovar for the rare materials needed to create their legendary weapons, such as Krummul Orcslayer's Setzunklufa.

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +15%.

Idea 5: The Titanium Guardians

In ages past Gor Vazumbrog had many guardians. The most famous of these were neither heroes nor guardsmen but the tall unyielding sentinels made from the namesake metal of the Titanium Hold. The golems of Gor Vazumbrog were stalwart sentinels made to face the most daunting and fearsome of tasks.

Cast from Titanium and adorned in protective runes, the golems were resistant to all manner of magic, perfect guardians of the cursed relics sealed deep in Vazumbrog's vaults. Terrors in combat and tireless in guardianship, the golems kept many roles - vault guardians, gatekeepers, and heavy support for dwarven troops facing goblin and orc incursions into their territory.

Effects: Fort maintenance modifier: -15%.

Idea 6: Krummul Orcslayer

Originally a dwarf of unknown origin, Krummul Orcslayer joined the Dauvek Veker at the unprecedented age of 23, having personally slain a nest of Deep Crows, bird-like insects of an unknown but likely horrible origin. From his early noteworthy actions his legend would only grow, he earned the name "Orcslayer" for his actions single-handedly slaying an entire orc warband over the course of but one month, and famously relieved the orcish siege of Hul-Jorkad, saving his fellow dwarves with the might of his two-handed greatsword "Setzunklufa", Skycleaver.

Over the course of his life, Krummul Orcslayer would put his experiences and thoughts into words and compile a comprehensive list of grudges and wrongdoings done to dwarvenkind by its enemies over the millennia, aptly named "Krummul Orcslayer's Book of Dwarven Grudges." In time, old age did what no other enemy of dwarf-kind could, and Orcslayer became one of only a handful of the Dauvek Veker to die of old age, a fact which is said to have infuriated the great warrior to his last breath.

Effects: Shock damage: +10%.

Idea 7: Dragon in the Deep

In the year 472, Gor Vazumbrog was unmade. It was not a goblin horde nor an orc warband that felled this mighty fortress, but something far more potent and far more unexpected. On a day like any other, with no warning given, The Hunter of the Deep keep came upon Vazumbrog. A great dragon of deepest purple scales, it tunnelled into the hold from its deepest levels, circumventing the Titanium Hold's many defences and killing all who stood in its path. Its corrosive breath ravaged flesh and melted the titanium golems sent against it, while its mere presence maddened and dazed the dwarves that it came upon.

The beast killed tens of thousands before the General-King admitted the hold could not be saved. Sending the remaining Titanium Guardians against the dragon in a desperate bid to buy time, the King ordered an abandonment of the lower levels and began to organise the total evacuation of all dwarves in Vazumbrog. While the refugees fled to the other holds of the Segbandal and prepared to regroup and retake their home, the dragon settled into its new home.

The bottom levels of the hold soon became saturated with gaseous poison, which mixed with the virulent magices of the innumerable cursed artifacts in the deep vaults to create The Dragon's Wound, a glowing purple miasma that leeched the spirit and melted the flesh, a permanent stain on reality commemorating the tragedy and hubris of the Titanium Hold.

Effects: Army leader maneuver: +1; Army morale recovery speed: +10%.

Ambition: Titanium Ambition

Effect: Stability cost modifier: -15%.
